findings.title: Backup code alone logs in without a password when any totpCode is sent
findings.body:
Line 121 only checks the password when `credentials.totpCode` is falsy (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`). The new backup-code branch at line 131 runs before the TOTP branch and never looks at `totpCode`.

So a request to the credentials provider with `email`, any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "1"), and one valid `backupCode` skips the password check, passes the backup-code check, and returns an authenticated user. A leaked backup code (they are offered as a downloadable txt file) is then enough to take over a CAL-password account, which defeats the purpose of a second factor.

Fix: always verify the password for CAL users regardless of `totpCode`, or at least reject requests that carry a backupCode with a totpCode and require password verification on the backup-code path.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body:
The code reads the encrypted backup-code array, finds the index in memory, nulls it, and writes the whole re-encrypted blob back. Nothing makes this atomic: no transaction, no conditional update, no version check.

- Two concurrent logins with the same code both pass the `indexOf` check and both succeed, so a single-use code can be used twice.
- Two concurrent logins with different codes each null their own index on the same stale copy. The last writer wins and restores the other, already-used code to valid.

Use a conditional update (e.g. `updateMany` where `backupCodes` equals the value that was read, then fail if count is 0) or a serializable transaction.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves UI out of sync and step stale
findings.body:
After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called. It now only runs when the user clicks "Close" on the new DisplayBackupCodes step. 2FA is already enabled on the server at this point.

If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (Escape or overlay click, both handled by `onOpenChange`), then:
- `onEnable` never fires, so the parent never refreshes and the 2FA switch keeps showing "disabled".
- `resetState` never runs, so `step` stays `DisplayBackupCodes`. Reopening the modal from the (wrong) unchecked switch lands directly on the old backup codes screen.

Either call `onEnable` (or a refresh) as soon as enable succeeds, or handle `onOpenChange` on this step the same way as Close.

findings.title: Backup code input not normalized for case/whitespace
findings.body:
Codes are generated as lowercase hex (`randomBytes(5).toString('hex')`). The input only strips dashes before an exact `indexOf` match. The same applies in disable.ts line 61.

The input placeholder is "XXXXX-XXXXX" (uppercase), and users commonly paste with leading or trailing whitespace. Either case makes a valid code fail with "Backup code is incorrect."

Apply `.trim().toLowerCase()` (and drop all non-hex characters) before comparing.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message points to a settings feature that doesn't exist
findings.body:
The message reads "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR adds no UI or endpoint to generate or regenerate backup codes. `setup.ts` refuses to run when 2FA is already enabled, so the only path is to disable and re-enable 2FA.

This error is mainly hit on the login page by users who enabled 2FA before this change. They cannot reach settings at all, so the message gives instructions they cannot follow.

Separately, once all codes are consumed the stored array is all nulls and still truthy. Those users get "incorrect backup code" instead of this message.

findings.title: Assertion on un-awaited promise always passes; backup-code login/disable untested
findings.body:
`expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on a Promise object, which is always truthy. The PR adds a FIXME acknowledging this instead of fixing it (e.g. `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`).

With the new flow, the dialog in this test stays open on the backup-codes screen and `onEnable` is never triggered. The broken assertion hides that.

The core new behavior (logging in with a backup code, single-use consumption, disabling 2FA with a backup code) also has no test; it is left as a TODO at line 12.

findings.title: Backup codes stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed
findings.body:
Backup codes only ever need to be verified, never displayed again. Yet they are stored with `symmetricEncrypt` under the shared `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so anyone with DB access plus that key can recover every user's plaintext codes.

Storing a salted hash per code (and deleting the matching hash on use) is the standard approach. It would also remove the decrypt/re-encrypt round-trip on every login.

findings.title: tabIndex=-1 removes keyboard access to password visibility toggle
findings.body:
This shared `PasswordField` is used across the app. Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide password button means keyboard-only and screen-reader users can no longer reach the toggle.

This is an accessibility regression unrelated to the backup-code feature.

findings.title: Copy button throws or falsely reports success when clipboard API unavailable
findings.body:
`navigator.clipboard` is undefined in non-secure contexts, e.g. a self-hosted instance served over plain http. There, `navigator.clipboard.writeText` throws a TypeError synchronously.

When the API does exist, the returned promise is not awaited, so the "Backup codes copied!" toast is shown even if the write is rejected.

Await the promise, catch errors, and only show the success toast when the write actually succeeded.
